name: Own It
definition: We solve problems, go the extra mile, and always think long-term. We're intentional about how we use our resources to drive success.

rows.situation: When a problem has no owner
rows.under: Flags it, and waits for someone to be assigned.
rows.justRight: Takes it, solves it, and gets a permanent owner named so it does not drift back.
rows.over: Collects unowned problems until your own commitments start slipping.

rows.situation: When the fast answer costs something later
rows.under: Takes the fast answer. Later is someone else's quarter.
rows.justRight: Names what later costs, and takes the option that is still right in two years.
rows.over: Optimizes for a long term so distant that this year's business is not served.

rows.situation: When the work is technically finished
rows.under: Hands it over at the line, and leaves the last gap sitting.
rows.justRight: Goes the extra step that makes it genuinely usable by the person receiving it.
rows.over: Gold-plates every handover, and the next piece of work never starts.

rows.situation: When the resource is the company's and not yours
rows.under: Spends it as though it were free, because the budget exists.
rows.justRight: Spends it the way you would spend your own, deliberately and for a reason you could defend.
rows.over: Refuses spend that would obviously pay for itself, and the team works around a gap that costs more.

rows.situation: When the thing you owned failed
rows.under: Points at the conditions and at the people upstream.
rows.justRight: Owns the outcome and the repair, and says what you will do differently.
rows.over: Takes the blame so completely that the systemic cause is never examined.

rows.situation: When your market wins and the group loses
rows.under: Takes the local win, and lets the group absorb the cost.
rows.justRight: Weighs both, and says openly when your own number is the one that should give.
rows.over: Defers to the group on everything, and stops running your own business.
